title: Examen civique and A2 level French: what changed in 2026 for your residence card
shortAnswer: Short answer: since 1 January 2026, anyone applying for a carte de séjour pluriannuelle (2 to 4 years) for the first time has to pass the examen civique and prove A2 level French. For a first carte de résident, valid 10 years, the requirement is B1. Both tests are taken before you file your application.

headers: Card you are applying for the first time

blocks.text: The examen civique and the French certificate are two separate tests: passing one does not replace the other.
What is the examen civique like?

It is 40 multiple-choice questions, in French, in 45 minutes. To pass you need at least 32 correct answers (80%). The questions cover the values of the Republic, its institutions, its history and everyday life in France.

items: Anyone only renewing a one-year card (salarié or étudiant, for example) without moving to the pluriannuelle.
Anyone renewing a carte pluriannuelle they already hold.
Some nationalities covered by their own agreements, such as Algerians.

blocks.text: Every case is individual: confirm your own situation with the préfecture or with an advisor before you file.

items: Work out your dates: if your one-year card expires in 2027 and you want to move to the pluriannuelle, start preparing for the tests now.
French: book a recognized exam (TCF, DELF) several weeks ahead; the places fill up.
Examen civique: practice with online tests in the official format. With a method, a few weeks is enough.
Contrat d'intégration républicaine (CIR): if you signed one when you arrived, the 24-hour civics training helps you for the exam.

items.question: What happens if I don't pass?
items.answer: You will not get the pluriannuelle with that application, but you can sit the test again. In the meantime, staying on a one-year card may still be possible if you meet its conditions.

items.question: Can I take the exam in my own language?
Does renewing my one-year card require it too?
items.answer: Not for renewing a one-year card on its own. It is required when you apply for the pluriannuelle or the carte de résident for the first time.
